symptoms: Severe acute malnutrition with severe dehydration or shock

management_steps.details: IM/IV administration. For IM: do not inject more than 1 g at one injection site. For IV: doses greater than 2 g must be given in two divided doses (i.e. 12 hourly), preferably by intravenous infusion over 30 minutes.

Neonates with severe dehydration / SAM with severe dehydration or shock / Bacillary dysentery in children < 12 months / Complicated SAM with danger signs: IM/IV, 100 mg/kg/dose immediately as a single dose (SAM with danger signs dose listed as 80 mg/kg/dose). Unsafe miscarriage: IV, 1 g as a single dose.
Always include dose and route in referral letter.

warnings: Avoid giving calcium-containing IV fluids (e.g. Ringers Lactate) together with ceftriaxone: if <= 28 days old, avoid calcium-containing IV fluids for 48 hours after ceftriaxone administered; if > 28 days old, give sequentially provided giving set is flushed thoroughly with sodium chloride 0.9% before and after.
